records.title: generative-media-skills
records.summary: A large provider-independent skill library for media production. Separate skills cover captions and accessibility, final QC and delivery, character continuity, audio mixing and generated-media QA, several with small validator scripts.
records.why_it_matters: It is the only candidate found that covers caption limits, delivery specs and character continuity in one place, with a caption validator that turns line length and reading speed into numbers.
records.fit_notes: Load single skills, not the whole library: each SKILL.md is 25-30 KB, so three of them fill a lot of context. The caption validator checks timing and line counts only; its own text says it does not judge accuracy, contrast or placement. The platform specs inside are dated by the author (verified 2026-07-10 in the text); re-check them before a paid ad delivery. I did not run any of its scripts. The README links to calesthio/OpenMontage, which is the same project as tool:openmontageinc/openmontage.

claims.text: Its caption skill runs a validator with a two-line limit, 42 characters per line and a warning above 20 characters per second.
claims.quote: python skills/production/audio-craft/captions-media-accessibility/scripts/validate_captions.py --max-lines 2 --max-chars-per-line 42 --cps-warning 20 captions_en.vtt
claims.locator: skills/production/audio-craft/captions-media-accessibility/SKILL.md, section on the bundled validator, example command

claims.text: Its delivery skill keeps at least 1 dB of true-peak headroom for web and social files when no target is given.
claims.quote: Leave at least 1 dB true-peak headroom for generic web/social delivery when no loudness target is specified; use the mandated loudness target for broadcast/streaming.

claims.text: Its continuity skill marks a character's features as locked, so they may not change across shots unless the user approves.
claims.quote: **Locked**: must remain constant unless user approves a redesign.

checked.what: captions-media-accessibility, media-qc-delivery and character-design-continuity SKILL.md files and the README against the three claims

records.title: claude-plugin-marketplace (ffmpeg-kinetic-captions)
records.summary: A Claude Code plugin marketplace. Its ffmpeg-effects plugin has a kinetic-captions skill: ASS subtitle tags for word-grow, karaoke and pop captions burned in with FFmpeg, with timing per platform.
records.why_it_matters: It gives exact word-pop timings and a reading-time formula, which is the kinetic-caption craft most other skills leave as 'make captions pop'.
records.fit_notes: Install only the ffmpeg-effects plugin; the marketplace holds many unrelated plugins. Its 50 px edge margin for 1080x1920 is far smaller than the platform UI zones in tool:openmontageinc/openmontage and tool:dojocodinglabs/remotion-superpowers, so captions placed by this rule can sit under TikTok buttons. The readability file credits its 1.5 s minimum and 42-character line to WCAG 2.2; I did not open WCAG to confirm that. The skill opens with Windows path rules unrelated to video.

related.note: 50 px edge margin vs 320 px bottom dead zone on TikTok
50 px edge margin vs captions 15-25% up from the bottom

claims.text: It gives word-grow timings per platform, for example 100-150 ms grow and 115-120% scale on TikTok.
claims.locator: plugins/ffmpeg-effects/skills/ffmpeg-kinetic-captions/SKILL.md, section Word-Grow Timing by Platform, table row TikTok

claims.text: Its reading-time rule holds a caption for at least 1.5 s, or word count at 160 words per minute.
claims.quote: duration = max(1.5, (word_count / 160) * 60)

claims.text: For mobile readability it asks for 50 px safe margins from the edges.
claims.quote: - Use safe margins (50px from edges)

checked.what: ffmpeg-kinetic-captions SKILL.md and caption-readability.md against the three claims

records.title: claude-video-vision
records.summary: A Claude Code plugin with an MCP server that extracts frames with ffmpeg and transcribes audio, so Claude can look at a video file. A /watch-video command and a video-perception skill drive it.
records.why_it_matters: It gives Claude eyes on a finished render, which any renderer's review loop can use when its own skill has no frame-inspection step.
records.fit_notes: It perceives, it does not judge: you still need a review checklist from another skill. The MCP server is fetched from npm by npx on first use, which runs remote code; pin a version or build from the repo if that matters. With the Gemini or OpenAI backend the audio leaves your machine; pick the local Whisper backend for client work. It also downloads YouTube videos with yt-dlp, which this lane did not assess.

claims.text: For a video over 30 s its command must run an analysis pass (scene changes, silence, transcription) before pulling frames.
claims.quote: 2. **REQUIRED for videos > 30s:** Call `video_analyze` BEFORE `video_watch`. This is NOT optional.

claims.text: The MCP server installs itself from npm through npx the first time it runs.
claims.quote: The MCP server will auto-install via `npx` from [npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/claude-video-vision) on first use — no build step required.

claims.text: With the Gemini backend the audio track is sent to Google.
claims.quote: - **Audio is sent to Google's Gemini API** via the endpoint `https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com`.

checked.what: README.md, commands/watch-video.md and PRIVACY.md against the three claims

records.title: motion-design skill (LottieFiles)
records.summary: A tool-agnostic motion design skill: director notes, easing and timing tables, patterns, and a quality checklist with severity tiers.
records.why_it_matters: Its checklist turns motion taste into checks an agent can tick before rendering, with a stated severity for each miss.
records.fit_notes: Written for UI motion first: some checks (prefers-reduced-motion, pausable animations over 5 s) do not apply to a rendered MP4; skip them. The checklist is for the agent to read code or frames against; the skill ships no tool that measures a render. Its ban on linear easing matches tool:haidrrrry/claude-remotion-skill.

claims.text: Its checklist caps the total stagger of a sequence below 500 ms and marks more as critical.
claims.quote: - [ ] Stagger total <500ms

claims.text: It allows at most a third of the elements on screen to move at the same time.
claims.quote: - [ ] 1/3 rule (density): max 1/3 elements active simultaneously

checked.what: quality-checklist.md and README.md against both claims

records.title: ffmpeg-skill
records.summary: An Agent Skill and MCP server of 42 local FFmpeg tools for cutting, captions, loudness and platform export, with a fixed probe, edit, check, verify, look workflow.
records.why_it_matters: It is the clearest delivery skill found: platform checks on the output file, numbers in the report, and a contact sheet the agent must view after any picture change.
records.fit_notes: Needs FFmpeg 6.1+ and Python 3.10+ locally; no cloud. It tells the agent to use only its scripts and never raw ffmpeg, so a job the 42 tools do not cover stops there. A good last step after any renderer: hand it the MP4 and ask for a platform check. I did not run it.

claims.text: Before reporting done, the agent checks the output against a named platform.
claims.quote: 5. **Check** with `check.py OUTPUT --platform X --expect-identity S:M`

claims.text: After any picture change it must view a tiled contact sheet, and say so when it could not look.
claims.quote: 8. **Look** after any picture change: `look.py OUTPUT --tiles 3x2`, view the PNG, name it in `Look:`;

claims.text: It burns caption words as written and never shortens them to fit.
claims.quote: - **The words in a caption** — burned as written; never rewrite or shorten them, even to "make it fit".
claims.locator: skills/ffmpeg-skill/SKILL.md, section on what the agent never changes

checked.what: skills/ffmpeg-skill/SKILL.md and README.md against the three claims

records.title: smooth-animation-skill
records.summary: A Claude Code skill for choppy code-rendered animation (HyperFrames, Remotion, canvas, three.js), with a script that measures repeated frames, stills and jitter in the file.
records.why_it_matters: It replaces 'looks choppy' with a measured number and a fixed order of fixes, and it re-measures the final file.
records.fit_notes: The only evidence is the author's own before/after on two films; treat the 0.1 jump limit as the author's threshold. Rendering at 60 fps with 3 blur samples costs render time; the skill says how to cut back. Its 'no still scenes' rule contradicts the calm holds other skills allow, so pick one rule set. I did not run the meter.

claims.text: It starts by measuring the current file and keeping the result.
claims.quote: **1. Measure the current file and keep the result**

claims.text: It sets a jitter limit: frame-to-frame motion change above 0.1 fails.
claims.quote: `jump` compares the amount of motion from one frame to the next. Measured in tests: smooth videos stay between 0.003 and 0.04, and videos with camera jitter between 0.27 and 0.6; the limit is 0.1.
claims.locator: SKILL.md, section on reading the meter

claims.text: It renders at a true 60 fps by default instead of interpolating frames.
claims.quote: **4. Render at a real 60 fps.** It is the default, not the last resort.

checked.what: SKILL.md and README.md against the three claims

records.title: OpenMontage
records.summary: An agent-driven video production system with staged skills: proposal, scene plan, edit, compose, each followed by a reviewer pass. Creative skills hold typography, safe-zone, storytelling and sound numbers.
records.why_it_matters: Its reviewer skill makes every critical finding carry a concrete fix and bounds revision rounds, and its typography skill has per-platform vertical safe zones.
records.fit_notes: AGPL: if you change it and run it as a service, the licence asks you to publish your changes; read it before client or SaaS use. The repo also ships face-swap and avatar skills, which this hub does not cover; this record covers only reviewer.md and the creative skills. Its two-round review bound is lower than the three rounds in tool:digitalsamba/claude-code-video-toolkit. The safe-zone table cites a third-party site; I did not open it.

related.note: 320 px bottom dead zone vs 50 px edge margin

claims.text: Any critical finding forces a revision and a re-review, at most two rounds.
claims.quote: | 1+ critical findings | **Revise** — fix all critical findings, then re-review (max 2 rounds). |

claims.text: It lists the dead zones of the TikTok UI on a 1080x1920 frame: 108 px top, 320 px bottom, 120 px right.
claims.locator: skills/creative/typography.md, Platform-Specific Safe Zones (Vertical 1080x1920), row TikTok

claims.text: The project is under the GNU AGPL version 3.
claims.quote: GNU AFFERO GENERAL PUBLIC LICENSE Version 3, 19 November 2007

checked.what: skills/meta/reviewer.md, skills/creative/typography.md, README.md and LICENSE against the three claims; the git tree listing for the face-swap skill

records.title: marketingskills (video, product-demo-recording)
records.summary: A marketing skill set; its video skill has a reference for recording a scripted product demo with Playwright: subtitle bar, step badge, a fake visible cursor and optional TTS.
records.why_it_matters: Screen demos are the most common developer clip, and this reference fixes their usual tells: an invisible cursor, captions covering the click, a blank first frame.
records.fit_notes: It tells the agent to set bypassCSP on the browser context and, on a non-localhost host, to drop the Secure cookie flag for the recording run. Do that only on a local or staging build, never against production. It also tells the agent never to take an API key pasted into chat, which is the opposite of the video-use README. The TTS step needs a paid key.

claims.text: It injects a fake cursor so viewers can see each click.
claims.quote: Playwright fires DOM events with no visible pointer, so viewers can't see what got clicked. Inject a fake cursor element and wrap clicks and fills in helpers:

claims.text: It sizes each scene caption at 50-80 characters.
claims.quote: - **Captions of 50-80 characters** read well and keep pauses short

claims.text: It switches off the page's content security policy in the recording browser.
claims.quote: A `style-src 'self'` policy without `unsafe-inline` blocks the inline styles on the subtitle bar and cursor. Keep `bypassCSP: true` on the context.

records.title: remotion-superpowers
records.summary: A plugin on top of the official Remotion skills that adds voiceover, music, footage, caption presets and a /review-video command that scores a render.
records.why_it_matters: Its review command does a cheap local frame check first, then a scored AI watch of the full render, and tells the agent to trust its own frames when they disagree.
records.fit_notes: The full review uploads your render to TwelveLabs, and voice and music use ElevenLabs: paid keys and your video leaves the machine. Step 1 alone (local stills) is free and works without either. Its caption placement agrees with tool:openmontageinc/openmontage and contradicts the 50 px margin in tool:josiahsiegel/claude-plugin-marketplace. Remotion's company licence applies as for tool:remotion-dev/skills.

claims.text: Review starts with a local check of rendered stills, then has TwelveLabs watch and score the full render.
claims.quote: Starts with a cheap local check of rendered still frames, then has TwelveLabs watch the full render and score it against a JSON rubric

claims.text: When the AI review and the agent's own frames disagree on something visible, the frames win.
claims.quote: Cross-check the AI review against your own frame check from step 1; if they disagree on something visible, trust the frames and say so.

claims.text: On 1080x1920 shorts it puts captions 15-25% up from the bottom to clear the platform UI.
claims.quote: | TikTok / Reels / Shorts (1080x1920) | About 15-25% up from the bottom (`bottom` around 300-480), or dead center for punchy hooks |

checked.what: skills/review-video/SKILL.md and rules/captions-workflow.md against the three claims

records.title: motion-skills (iArt)
records.summary: An index of 19 motion-graphics skill packs plus a small verify toolkit: seek-and-screenshot, a contact sheet of start, middle and end, and an MP4 spec probe.
records.why_it_matters: The verify scripts are a renderer-neutral review loop: look at three frames on one sheet, then assert resolution, codec, fps and duration of the file.
records.fit_notes: The skills themselves live in 19 other repos; this record covers only the index and tools/verify. The README promotes the vendor's paid iArt agent and cites its own cost figures; I did not check them. The scripts need ffmpeg, and Playwright Chromium for HTML; I did not run them.

claims.text: After stills are tiled, the agent inspects the sheet against the brief for clipped or off-canvas text.
claims.quote: # inspect sheet.png: matches the brief? clipped text / off-canvas / FOUC?

claims.text: It asserts a vertical short's real resolution and frame rate from the encoded file.
claims.quote: scripts/probe-mp4.sh out/short.mp4 1080x1920 30      # vertical short contract
claims.locator: tools/verify/README.md, Usage by tier, Heavy Remotion

checked.what: tools/verify/README.md and README.md against both claims

records.title: motion-graphics (Mort1d)
records.summary: A skill that directs, animates, scores and renders a promo or reel from HTML scenes in headless Chrome, with sub-frame motion blur and an original score on the same beat grid.
records.why_it_matters: It fixes a master spec, forbids copying reference material, and makes the agent critique until every score is 8 or more before the final render.
records.fit_notes: No npm packages or API keys per its compatibility line; needs Node 22.4+, ffmpeg and a Chromium browser. The SKILL.md is 35 KB. Its -1 dBTP ceiling is looser than the -1.5 dBTP in tool:mattypark/motion-graphics-skill. The critique score is the agent grading itself; nothing independent checks it. I did not run it.

claims.text: It sets the master: 60 fps, H.264 and AAC, -14 LUFS, true peak at or below -1 dBTP.
claims.quote: the master (1920×1080 or the chosen format, 60 fps, H.264 + AAC, -14 LUFS, true peak ≤ -1 dBTP)

claims.text: It forbids copying footage, frames, music or a recognisable design from a reference.
claims.quote: Never copy footage, frames, music or a recognisable design from a reference

claims.text: It critiques until every score is 8 or more, then renders and runs QA.
claims.quote: ### 7. Critique until every score is 8+, then render + QA

checked.what: skills/motion-graphics/SKILL.md and README.md against the three claims

records.title: motion-video-director (mattypark)
records.summary: A skill for code-drawn motion graphics and edited videos with a fixed intake, storyboard and preview flow, plus stock, SFX, font and Lottie sourcing through MCPs and APIs.
records.why_it_matters: It is the candidate with the most explicit asset rules: a manifest with source and licence for every downloaded file, and no font shipped without a verified licence.
records.fit_notes: Asset search needs Pixabay, Freesound and Firecrawl keys. It adds the Playwright MCP through npx with @latest, which runs whatever version is newest; pin a version. It uses Pinterest, Behance and Dribbble for style references and says reference-only unless licensed; check that the agent keeps to that. The SKILL.md is 53 KB.

claims.text: It records licence and attribution for every downloaded asset in a manifest.
claims.quote: Record license/attribution for every downloaded asset in `manifest.json`.

claims.text: It never ships a font whose licence it could not verify.
claims.quote: Never ship a font whose license you couldn't verify.

claims.text: It installs the Playwright MCP from npm at its newest version.
claims.quote: "playwright": { "command": "npx", "args": ["@playwright/mcp@latest"
claims.locator: skills/motion-video-director/SKILL.md, setup table, row MCP Playwright
